text.p: Investors should hold shares of Polish drug maker Jelfa SA in the short term and buy them in the long term, the brokerage unit of Bank Handlowy brokerage said in a report released to the press on Tuesday.
It said short-term investors should hold Jelfa despite its previous steep share-price rise. Jelfa rose 55.4 percent from May 30 to September 17 this year.

"To short-term investors, we recommend holding shares of Jelfa, despite the recent significant growth in their price," the report, dated October 11, said. Jelfa shares closed at 46 zlotys on the Warsaw bourse on October 11.
On Tuesday Jelfa was flat at 40 zlotys.
Handlowy said Jelfa was a long-term buy because of its strong domestic market position in ointments and creams and its high export level to CIS countries.
It said Jelfa's conducted and planned investment, seen at 180 million zlotys from 1993 to 1998, would lead to greater efficiency in production and a decline in costs.

But it said pharmaceutical firms in Hungary, Croatia and Western Europe provided strong competition and that Jelfa would be hurt by a government delay in lifting price controls and an underutilisation of production capacity, now at 50-60 percent.
Handlowy said Jelfa would lift net profit to 20.5 million zlotys this year and 26.5 million zlotys next year from 13.6 million zlotys in 1995.
It said Jelfa would up sales to 146 million zlotys this year and 176.5 million next year from 128.8 million in 1995.
